lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Education leads the page instead of the embedded software experience.
The listed dates leave about 10 months between graduation and the first job without study or work shown.
“Update speed” does not identify what improved by 60%.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it means download time, total update time or transfer rate.

items.says: The test count describes the rig’s workload but not what running it accomplished.
items.because: Tests per build establish scope, not whether the rig caught regressions or changed validation.

items.says: The wording attributes the diagnosis to the saved data rather than to its use.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture that component without aliasing.
items.because: An 8 kHz sampling rate has a 4 kHz Nyquist frequency, so the component aliases to 3 kHz.

items.says: The fault-detector clause gives an intended benefit, not an observed result.
Declaring the shared counter volatile does not, by itself, fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make counter operations atomic, so the interrupt handler and main loop can still interleave their accesses.

items.says: The claimed race-condition fix has no observable symptom or verification attached.
“The counter” is repeated unnecessarily.
The motor-controller rewrite and its results are also credited to a project that ended before this job began.
items.because: The Formula Student entry describes a roughly 300-robot fleet with equivalent jitter and fault reductions.

items.says: The strongest Voltline result is buried at the end of the entry.
items.because: The fleet size, jitter reduction and fault reduction establish the role’s scope and impact immediately.

items.says: “Rewrote” does not identify what changed in the motor controller.
“Automated end-of-line tests” does not show what you built or changed.
The solder-paste conclusion appears without the diagnostic step that established it.
The sentence makes the findings, rather than a person, the actor that updated the reflow profile.
The calibration-procedure bullet does not say what in the procedure addressed drift.
“15 to 2 a quarter” expresses the complaint rate awkwardly.
The opening phrase is promotional jargon rather than an identifiable engineering contribution.
items.because: It neither names the station plainly nor shows a design decision you made.

items.says: The claim about redefining sensing does not identify a change or benefit for users.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the project’s value from the broad claim.

items.says: The measured current reduction should lead the project instead of the broad opening claim.
items.because: It immediately shows both impact and the sleep-and-batching decisions behind it.

items.says: “Openly” adds little to the publication claim.
The robot-fleet work is incorrectly attributed to the Formula Student electric-car project.
items.because: The project ended in 2021, while the warehouse-robot role began in 2023.

items.says: “Worked on firmware and testing” says neither what the work produced nor what changed.
items.because: The reader cannot connect the activity to a result.

items.says: The bullet does not identify a firmware change or test you owned.
items.because: “Firmware and testing” spans multiple tasks, and “Worked on” conceals your action.

items.says: The dashboard CAN-bus work stops at the activity rather than its result.
The passive construction hides who wrote and tested the dashboard firmware.
“Tested against the motor controller” does not identify what CAN-bus behavior was checked.
The identifiable student-car bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: The dashboard work fits the electric-car heading, whereas the surrounding robot-fleet bullets conflict with the project dates.

items.says: The fleet size and improvements repeat results credited to the later Voltline role.
items.because: The roughly 300-robot fleet, eightfold jitter reduction and fault reduction of more than half correspond to the Voltline figures.

items.says: The rewrite claim does not identify the change responsible for the reported improvements.
items.because: “Rewrote” does not show what engineering decision produced the result.

items.says: The motor-fault reduction does not say what faults were counted over.
items.because: “More than half” lacks the count or period needed to interpret the proportion.
